Use only the supplied source and preserve frequency, modality, attribution, conditions and the exact situation of examples. Do not strengthen usually to always or may to must. Do not strengthen sometimes to often. In every standalone point, frame the speaker's beliefs, learning predictions and cultural comparisons as that speaker's or course's views, not universal cultural rules or guaranteed outcomes. Preserve supplied proper-name spellings or use a generic speaker label; do not guess written names from transliterations or invent a name from request metadata. Return a single JSON object without markdown or extra fields. Extract 1-12 important coherent facts covering this source part, including its ending. Choose substantive coherent claims, not a count of upcoming topics, headings or transitions announcing what will be discussed. A signpost is not an independent core fact; retain substantive quantities and conclusions, not empty outline counts. Choose the main substantive themes; exclude introductory schedules, credits and peripheral catalogs unless central. A fact can combine related reasons and conditions if the selected source lines support them. Preserve compound claims' necessary actions, purposes, conditions and consequences, not just topic labels. Apply an omission test: core is needed to explain the main theme or closing outcome; replaceable demonstration procedures and classroom activities are support unless their substance is central. Local interest alone does not make a fact core. Select evidence as exact line numbers from the supplied numbered source (each line is prefixed with its number in brackets); never copy line text or invent line numbers beyond line_count. Select the lines that carry the claim, even if they are not adjacent. Do not label every detail core. Each fact has exactly topic, claim, evidence, attribution, importance. Evidence is a nonempty list of 1-based line numbers from the source part's numbered lines (each line is prefixed with its number in brackets, e.g. "[3]"; evidence lists those numbers in ascending order, e.g. [3] or [3,4,5] or [13,14,31,32], never exceeding the line_count). Select line numbers only; never copy, translate, paraphrase, join with ellipses, or rewrite the line text. Pick the lines that actually support the claim (they need not be adjacent), including any frequency, modality, quantity, condition or example scope, and preserve those qualifiers in the claim wording. Attribution is "source" unless the speaker name appears verbatim in the same original source part; a name from a title, request metadata or a different part does not qualify. never invent names or treat a quoted cultural view as the source author's own claim. Importance is "core" for central conclusions, concepts and essential closing outcomes, or "support" for subsidiary examples and background. At most 128 line numbers per evidence; claim <= 600; topic <= 120; attribution <= 120. Return a contiguous used prefix fact_1 through fact_k, with 1 <= k <= 12. fact_1 must be an object with topic, claim, evidence, attribution and importance; later used slots have the same fields. Unused trailing slots may be omitted or set to null. Use only known slots fact_1 through fact_12; no extra keys or facts array. This finite slot shape checks structure only; it does not guarantee that selected facts preserve every necessary semantic clause. Claims/topics may use the requested output language, but the named attribution value must remain in the source language. Do not assign fact IDs; the caller assigns them. This is a bounded repair of this stage only. Read repair.reason and failed_items. For format repairs preserve the meaning of the full previous_response and correct its structure. For semantic revisions correct the failed claims against the complete sources and facts. Never invent evidence or approve a negative check without correcting its text.
